questions.q: What causes the overestimation bias in vanilla DQN's target computation?
options: Taking the max over the target network's noisy Q-value estimates is statistically biased toward overestimated actions
The replay buffer stores too few transitions
The reward function is scaled incorrectly
Gamma is set too close to zero
questions.explain: Since Q-value estimates carry noise in both directions, the max operator systematically favors whichever estimate happens to be overestimated, inflating the target.

questions.q: How does Double DQN compute its target differently from vanilla DQN?
options: It removes the target network entirely
The online network selects the best next action; the target network evaluates that specific action's Q-value
It uses two separate replay buffers
It doubles the learning rate
questions.explain: Double DQN decouples action selection (done by the online network) from action evaluation (done by the target network), which reduces the correlation that drives overestimation.

questions.q: In a Dueling DQN architecture, what does the value stream V(s) represent?
options: The reward received at the current timestep
A single scalar estimating how good the overall state is, independent of any specific action
The probability of each action being optimal
The replay buffer's current size
questions.explain: The value stream outputs one scalar per state describing its overall value, separate from the per-action advantage stream.

questions.q: Why does Dueling DQN subtract the mean advantage when recombining V(s) and A(s, a) into Q(s, a)?
options: To make the Q-values negative
To keep V(s) and A(s, a) individually identifiable instead of drifting by an arbitrary offsetting constant
Because it is required by the replay buffer
To implement the target network sync
questions.explain: Without subtracting the mean advantage, V(s) and A(s,a) could each drift by an arbitrary constant that cancels out in the sum, which destabilizes training; subtracting the mean removes that ambiguity.

questions.q: Are Double DQN and Dueling DQN mutually exclusive techniques?
options: Yes, a DQN implementation must choose only one
No, they address independent weaknesses (the target computation and the network architecture) and are commonly combined
Yes, Dueling DQN replaces the need for a target network
No, but combining them is mathematically invalid
questions.explain: Double DQN changes how the TD target is computed, while Dueling DQN changes the network's architecture. They address unrelated issues and are routinely used together.
